clue.text: Lady carries on in Italy with two gentlemen?

indicators.note: a person who carries something holds it within, so the name holds the next word inside it

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name, standing in for any lady

explanation.surface: A woman goes about her business in Italy escorted by a pair of gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Shakespeare's play The Two Gentlemen of Verona, so the place in Italy is the one those two gentlemen come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy The Two Gentlemen of Verona sets its pair of heroes in this Italian city.

clue.text: Sour-tasting wine from France, say, ray rejected

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so the letters of the word ray are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A French wine has turned sour and is sent back by someone called Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is a loose anagram signal here, thrown out of order, not a turnaround: read backwards the fish would not fit the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasting acidic like soured wine is having a sharp, tart flavour.

clue.text: Rodney went round gallery, went round and round

indicators.note: went round means the name surrounds the gallery's letters

parts.note: Rod is short for Rodney
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Rodney toured an art gallery, walking in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The TATE is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun about an axis, turning in circles, is what revolved means.

clue.text: Gruel Nina's mixed not accepted initially by baby

indicators.note: mixed means the remaining letters are stirred up into a new order
not shows a letter is left out of the pool
initially asks for the opening letter of the word accepted

explanation.surface: Nina has made porridge that the baby refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not accepted initially' removes A from GRUEL NINAS; 'mixed' rearranges the other nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant still being nursed or suckled is a baby.

clue.text: It is instrumental in telling you how far you have travelled

definitions.text: It is instrumental in telling you how far you have travelled

parts.words: It is instrumental in telling you how far you have travelled
parts.note: instrumental is used literally: the thing is a dashboard instrument that measures distance covered

explanation.definitionFit: A car's mileage gauge is the instrument that records the distance a vehicle has covered.

clue.text: Prevent one from making their mark in the election

definitions.text: Prevent one from making their mark in the election

parts.words: Prevent one from making their mark in the election
parts.note: making their mark reads as succeeding, but literally means putting a cross on a ballot paper

explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone of the right to vote stops them marking a ballot.

clue.text: Obscure retreat on way to middle

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the next
to retreat is to go backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: obscure means dim, hard to see
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A secretive withdrawal on the road towards the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' says the word for obscure goes backwards; in a down clue 'on' means sitting above the abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre or heart of something is its midst.

clue.text: Representative serving as a model

definitions.meaning: representative as an adjective, standing for its class
serving as a model or exemplar of a kind

explanation.definitionFit: Characteristic of its kind, a standard example both represents and exemplifies the type.

clue.text: Dairy built above hospital in city

indicators.note: above puts the rearranged letters on top of the next piece in this down clue
built means constructed, so the letters are assembled into a new shape

explanation.surface: A dairy has been constructed over a hospital in town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saudi Arabian capital is a large Middle Eastern city.

clue.text: Still replacing pole in old capital

parts.note: still means constant, unchanging

indicators.note: replacing means putting back in a different place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is still put in place of a pole in a former capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Byzantine and Ottoman seat of power was renamed Istanbul and lost capital status to Ankara.

clue.text: No riotous extravaganza that's disreputable

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an extravaganza is a wild, free-form show, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy, over-the-top party gives everyone a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riotous' looks like it describes the extravaganza, but it is the word that gets shaken up, with 'extravaganza' as the signal and No kept unchanged in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone infamous, known widely for bad deeds, is disreputable.

clue.text: Do exercise before you initially become stupefied

indicators.note: before places the exercise letters ahead of the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word you

explanation.surface: An instruction to work out before you start feeling dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dazed and slow-witted, as if drugged, is the stupefied state the word describes.

clue.text: Cowardly Leslie's passage in the lead

indicators.note: in the lead puts the passage at the front, ahead of the name

parts.note: the gut is the alimentary passage through the body
Les is short for Leslie, so Leslie's becomes LES'S, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A timid man named Leslie is put at the front of a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leslie's' is shortened to Les's; the apostrophe drops out, leaving the letters LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking guts, or courage, describes a cowardly person.

clue.text: Saw cake hadn't been decorated

parts.note: hadn't gives the negative not
a cake that has been decorated has been iced

explanation.surface: Someone spotted that a cake had been left plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a noun or the past of seeing a cake; it is the definition, and the cake supplies the context for icing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have seen something is to have observed or spotted it.

clue.text: More than one spoke to the circle

definitions.text: More than one spoke to the circle

parts.words: More than one spoke to the circle
parts.note: spoke looks like speech to a group, but it means the lines running from centre to rim of a circle, in the plural

explanation.definitionFit: Lines from a circle's centre to its circumference, plural of the Latin-derived geometric term, are like wheel spokes.

clue.text: A singer included first piece of music quivering

indicators.note: included means the singer holds another letter within it

parts.note: a treble is a boy singer with a high voice

indicators.note: first piece of asks for the opening letter of the word music

explanation.surface: A choirboy took part in the opening number, shaking with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shaking or trembling is to quiver, a literary adjective formed like afloat.

clue.text: Illusory discovery in horse's home?

parts.note: a mare is a female horse, so horse's gives mare's
a nest is a home for birds

explanation.surface: A supposed find in a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of mare's drops out, leaving MARES.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a supposed find that proves false, or a chaotic muddle.

clue.text: Bar Alex felling large plant

indicators.note: felling means knocking down, so the letters of the name are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: a tree is a large plant

explanation.surface: Alex is chopping down a big tree in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed rod on which wheels turn is a bar.

clue.text: Shining on resort

parts.note: shining means bright
taken as written

explanation.surface: The sun is shining on a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sussex town is a well-known English seaside holiday destination.

clue.text: Noisy stocktaker?

parts.note: stocktaker hints at an inventory clerk but means someone who takes livestock, a cattle thief, and the word also suggests something that makes a crackling noise

explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief takes stock literally, and the word also names something that crackles like leaves.

clue.text: Remove more hair from one's body?

definitions.text: Remove more hair from one's body?

parts.words: Remove more hair from one's body?
parts.note: describes going through hair removal with hot wax a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Depilating with hot wax again means treating the skin a second time.

clue.text: We called in number during noisy dispute

indicators.note: during means the pieces come in the middle of the other word

parts.note: taken as written
called in, as on the phone, means rang
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: We phoned in a figure in the middle of a loud row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called in' is phone-call language; 'during' sends the ringing and the Roman fifty into the middle of the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that is long and noisy is a quarrel.

clue.text: Think it is correct to look healthy

parts.note: to look is to see
fit means healthy

explanation.surface: Deciding it is right to appear in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem something proper or suitable is to judge it right.

clue.text: Piles on unfortunate character from abroad

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hapless foreigner suffering from haemorrhoids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' shuffles only PILES; ON stays as written after it. 'character' means a letter, here one of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet is a foreign written symbol.

clue.text: Topless drunk is game

indicators.note: topless means the top letter is removed, which in a down clue is the first

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk without a shirt is fair game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' removes the first letter of BLOTTO, slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style bingo played with numbered counters is a game of chance.

clue.text: Army long time captive

parts.note: a host is an old word for an army or great multitude
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Soldiers keep a prisoner for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held by captors as security for a demand is a prisoner.

clue.text: Bone reported in undercut of beef

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: to bone a fish is to fillet it, removing the skeleton

explanation.surface: A butcher tells of a bone found in a tender joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undercut' is the British butcher's word for the tenderloin, the cut sold in French as this.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-named tenderloin steak comes from the beef undercut beneath the ribs.

clue.text: One gets taken for a ride

definitions.text: One gets taken for a ride

parts.words: One gets taken for a ride
parts.note: taken for a ride suggests being swindled, but literally means being carried along as a traveller

explanation.definitionFit: A traveller carried in a vehicle by someone else is literally conveyed on a journey.

clue.text: Pto some part of the company report?

definitions.meaning: Pto is the abbreviation printed at the foot of a page asking the reader to flip it

definitions.text: some part of the company report?
definitions.meaning: a company's annual report states its total sales income for the year

explanation.definitionFit: PTO stands for please flip the page, and a firm's revenue figure in accounts goes by the same word.

clue.text: Gas foul, say, in summer on the continent

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the French word

parts.note: été is French for summer, written without accents
foul sounds like fowl, and a hen is an example of a fowl

explanation.surface: Gas gives off a foul smell during a European summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' is a sound-alike for fowl, and 'say' marks the hen as one example of fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethylene is a colourless hydrocarbon gas used to ripen fruit.
